transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-16 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Priya Nair, Carlos Mendes, Ava Lin (Redwood) — Dr. Emily Ross, Markus Hale, Sophie Nguyen, Ben Ortiz (StratosHealth)

Summary: Quick leadership brief to align on decisions that will ripple into product priorities and go-to-market for Q4. Focus on tightening latency SLOs for hosted API, clarifying private deployment commitments, and re-prioritizing hires to reinforce infra and SRE.

Topics covered: Q4 roadmap, SLA targets, private deployment resourcing, security/compliance asks from StratosHealth, pilot timelines, hiring pivot.

Action items (auto): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining right on time um this is the decision forge and clarity briefing, real quick goal — leave with three decisions and a set of owners, we'll try to be crisp, there will be questions after.
[00:12] Carlos: hey all, quick slide 0: we had three threads that kept coming up in calls this month — private infra asks, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and the SRE gap in light of recent incidents.
[00:25] Dr. Emily Ross: thanks uh Priya — I want to say upfront StratosHealth is excited, we've been running the hosted API in a pilot but our compliance folks are pushing hard for VPC or on-prem due to PHI/PII rules. this is the blocker for us to sign.
[00:43] Priya: noted, and that's the big lever. reminder: private isn't just a checkbox it's a resourcing and SLA commitment. Ava, quick framing on product impact?
[00:51] Ava: yeah so to be blunt, private deployments need a customer-managed control plane or our private control plane with KMS options, encryption in transit at rest, and audit logs — those ship with Redwood Private but we need more docs and a streamlined onramp for mid-size regulated orgs. we propose a templated playbook and a 3-week fast-track for pilots.
[01:15] Markus Hale: can you define "fast-track" — like what throughput and latency are guaranteed? our clinical workflows need sub-400ms median for conversational interactivity.
[01:28] Carlos: okay, we have internal benchmarks but many of them are for stealth configurations. rough guidance: for hosted small instances we're seeing p50 around 120-180ms for gpt-like small models at 32 seq lengths; private will vary by GPU class and quantization. we can commit to published profiles once we run a StratosHealth-specific benchmark.
[01:55] Sophie Nguyen: just to add, our data residency and audit chain are non-negotiable. also the KV cache behavior in partial cold-starts caused a regressive spike in first-token latency in last week's test.
[02:15] Carlos: mmh yeah the KV cache warmup is real — we have options: prefix caching, pre-warm pipelines, and a model-variant fallback to smaller quantized base to reduce first-token times. each has cost implications.
[02:35] Ben Ortiz: security question — for Private, will Redwood support our HSM/KMS provider via customer-owned keys or do you require Redwood-managed KMS? we need customer-managed keys due to audit.
[02:48] Ava: we already have an integration path for external KMS; the main gap is automating key rotation and providing the SAML SSO + RBAC templates for our installers. that's on our doc backlog, we'll move it up.
[03:05] Priya: decision #1: commit to producing a StratosHealth pilot package: private deployment playbook, KMS integration notes, and SOC2 artifact pointers. owner: Carlos + Ben (customer) to exchange artifacts. timeline: initial package by 2026-10-23. agreed?
[03:25] Dr. Emily Ross: that works, yes.
[03:29] Carlos: noted — I'll put the checklist in the shared drive and link in the follow up.
[03:35] Priya: decision #2 on SLA tightening: we propose a target of 99.9% availability for dedicated pools and a latency SLO band that depends on model class. recognize we need to quantify the cost delta. we want to tell enterprise customers what to expect.
[03:55] Ava: to operationalize that we need an infra hire — +1 SRE or infra eng focused on runtime optimizations, plus an SLO playbook. hiring team will reprioritize two reqs this week.
[04:12] Priya: hiring pivot is decision #3: shift next two hiring slots to infra/SRE (one senior, one IC) and delay one feature PM. HR and hiring ops to action.
[04:24] Markus Hale: rough ask — can you share the cost impact of 99.9% vs 99.95% availability? we need to map to our budget cycles.
[04:37] Carlos: sure we have a cost model spreadsheet, will include p95/p99 token cost deltas and suggested burst policies.
[04:45] Priya: okay now open Q&A — we'll rapid-fire the major items we heard in pre-reads.
[05:00] Sophie Nguyen: on the KV cache comment — do you have any mitigation for warmups that doesn't require pre-warming thousands of prefixes? that's operationally hard for us.
[05:12] Carlos: yeah, options — adaptive prefix caching (learned from workload), or just provide a warmed-inference node pool for the first hour of a clinical window. both approaches trade cost for user experience. transcription note: "inference node" was said hurriedly as "in furns node" earlier in an internal run.
[05:35] Dr. Emily Ross: are you going to support on-prem air-gapped installs? our legal folks prefer air gap for certain sites.
[05:45] Ava: we have a plan for on-prem packaging but it's higher effort; we can do air-gapped for selected customers with dedicated engineering time — propose a scoped 8-week engagement and deliverables list (installer, offline KMS setup doc, acceptance tests).
[06:05] Priya: timeline check — StratosHealth pilot kickoff target: 2026-11-01. can you commit?
[06:12] Markus Hale: tentative yes, pending internal sign-off on budget and SLAs.
[06:18] Priya: good. next up — incident retro brief: last month we had a 3-hour mid-latency regression due to a kernel scheduling issue on a particular GPU type. short version: we improved routing and changed the fallback policy.
[06:36] Carlos: contributes: we added graceful degradation to model routing so heavy queries fall back to lower-cost variants, reduced impact. but we owe a postmortem doc with timelines and mitigations. I'll own that.
[06:50] Ava: note to leadership: we also need better escalation playbooks and more robust tracing at token level to identify KV cache misses vs kernel stalls.
[07:05] Priya: okay switching to go-to-market alignment — sales ops flagged that several mid-market prospects stalled on pricing predictability. we need a clearer offering: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved pools, and private with clear engagement pricing.
[07:23] Dr. Emily Ross: for us pricing predictability is crucial. a pilot with transparent unit economics helps.
[07:30] Priya: we'll produce a two-pager: "Pilot economics for regulated customers". Owner: Priya + Product. deliverable by 2026-10-20.
[07:42] Markus Hale: question — will you publish model performance profiles (latency vs cost) for common sequence lengths? that's useful for capacity planning.
[07:52] Carlos: yes, that's part of the benchmark deliverable. expect a spreadsheet per model family and GPU type.
[08:03] Sophie Nguyen: security follow-up — does Redwood log token payloads in any central system? we need confirmation of zero retention of PHI-level content.
[08:15] Carlos: we have a no-content-retention policy for hosted by default, but for private deployments control is in the customer's hands. we will provide a signed attestation and config toggles for stripping payloads at the edge.
[08:33] Ben Ortiz: please include an explanation of your tracing hooks and how to redact payloads in instrumentation.
[08:40] Ava: will add a redaction appendix to the pilot docs.
[08:47] Priya: ok quick break into lightning updates from org leads — Ava, product?
[08:55] Ava: product updates — will freeze major API surface changes for the quarter except critical security fixes; focusing on stability, pilot-friendly UX, and rollout tooling (canary, A/B, fallback policies). we're also shipping SDK updates to reduce client-side latency by removing a blocking call in the JS SDK.
[09:18] Priya: Carlos, engineering ops?
[09:20] Carlos: priority is SRE hire, infra optimizations for batching and kernel selection heuristics, and better telemetry dashboards. we'll pilot token-level tracing on two clusters.
[09:33] Priya: leadership ask — we need a one-pager on what counts as "pilot success" for regulated accounts. Markus — what's success for you?
[09:41] Markus Hale: technical: pass of integration tests, median latency under 400ms in production window, audit logs + KMS keys in place; business: signed MSA and pilot budget committed.
[09:55] Priya: great. record decisions again quickly: 1) Pilot package (Carlos owns) by 10/23, 2) SLA posture and SRE hire (Ava + hiring ops) immediate, 3) hiring pivot to infra is approved.
[10:15] Dr. Emily Ross: a couple quick items from our side — we'll send compliance matrix and internal security contacts. expect those by Tuesday.
[10:24] Sophie Nguyen: and we'll run a short smoke test with a redacted dataset before the pilot to validate the KV cache pattern.
[10:31] Priya: timeline recap and next steps — see metadata for owners. we'll send minutes and links. any final escalations?
[10:40] Ben Ortiz: one last ask — can Redwood provide a list of personnel who will have emergency access to the private deployments for incident response? we need to include it in our vendor risk assessment.
[10:50] Ava: yes, we can produce an access roster template and limited-breakglass procedure.
[10:58] Priya: awesome. thank you everyone — end briefing. follow-up in email with attachments and calendar invites.

Notes about transcript quality: some words mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV" as "K-Vee", "kernel" as "kernell"), occasional speaker attribution drift where Redwood staff recorded as "Speaker 2" in the recording.

References shared: link: /drive/redwood/pilots/stratoshealth-pilot-brief.pdf (attaching in follow up), link: /drive/redwood/benchmarks/q4-latency-cost-model.xlsx (benchmarks spreadsheet)

End of transcript.
